$instance holds the resolved settings, secrets included: don't log or dump its settings.

Parameter Type Description $instance Channel_Instance The instance being edited, or the provisional one of a new channel. $channel Channel The module of the instance.

Fired in includes/admin/class-channel-form.php.

docs.title: sc_wpun_capability
docs.text:
Filter, since 2.0.0

Filters the capability needed to use the plugin's settings page.

It decides who sees the settings page, saves the settings, sends a test message and dismisses the plugin's notice. An empty or non-string value is ignored.

Lowering it hands every user with the capability control over where the plugin's notifications go. Such a user can:

  • send the update notifications, a list of the site's outdated and possibly vulnerable plugins and themes, to any address;
  • send test messages to any address;
  • change the From and Reply-To addresses;
  • add, edit, switch off, duplicate and delete channels;
  • hide the core update notice and run the update check on demand;
  • see the values of channel settings set in wp-config.php or by the environment when the field is not secret and its schema sets show_external.

Example, let editors manage the plugin:

add_filter( 'sc_wpun_capability', fn() => 'edit_pages' );
Parameter Type Description $capability string Capability. Default manage_options.

Fired in includes/admin/class-settings-page.php.

docs.title: sc_wpun_settings_tab_{tab}
docs.text:
Action, since 2.0.0

Draws a tab of the settings screen.

The dynamic part, $tab, is the tab's slug. Add the tab with the sc_wpun_settings_tabs filter; it is listed only while something is hooked here. Output inside the screen's wrapper.

Fired in includes/admin/class-settings-page.php.

docs.title: sc_wpun_settings_tabs
docs.text:
Filter, since 2.0.0

Filters the tabs of the settings screen.

A tab is shown only if something is hooked on sc_wpun_settings_tab_{$tab} to draw it. Entries whose slug is not a string equal to its sanitize_key() form, or whose label is not a string, are ignored. The General tab can not be removed.

Example, add a tab:

add_filter( 'sc_wpun_settings_tabs', fn( $tabs ) => $tabs + array( 'mine' => 'Mine' ) );
add_action( 'sc_wpun_settings_tab_mine', fn() => print '<p>Hello</p>' );
Parameter Type Description $tabs array<string, string> Tab labels keyed by slug. Default general and channels.

Fired in includes/admin/class-settings-page.php.

docs.title: sc_wpun_disable_cron
docs.text:
Action, since 1.0.0

Fires when the plugin is deactivated, to turn the scheduled check off.

Fired in includes/class-plugin.php, includes/class-scheduler.php.

docs.title: sc_wpun_loaded
docs.text:
Action, since 2.0.0

Fires when the plugin has loaded and its hooks are registered.

Add-ons can use it as the moment to start talking to the plugin's API.

Fired in includes/class-plugin.php.

docs.title: Actions you can fire
docs.text: The plugin listens to these actions but does not fire them itself. Call them with do_action().

docs.title: sc_wpun_enable_cron
docs.text:
Action, since 1.0.0

Schedules the update check. Handled by the Scheduler class.

Kept from 1.x. Schedules the check at the saved frequency, unless it is already scheduled at it. The plugin does this itself on every request (on init), so there is rarely a reason to call it. Pass a frequency to schedule at it instead of the saved one; manual stops the checks, as sc_wpun_disable_cron does.

do_action( 'sc_wpun_enable_cron' );
do_action( 'sc_wpun_enable_cron', 'daily' );
Parameter Type Description $frequency string Optional. A frequency key from sc_wpun_frequencies, such as daily, or manual. Default is the saved frequency.

Handled in includes/class-plugin.php.

docs.title: sc_wpun_run_check
docs.text:
Action, since 2.0.0

Runs the update check now.

It works as a scheduled run does: same routing, per-instance dedupe, delivery state and hooks, so items an instance was already told about are not sent again. The notification source is manual and the schedule is not changed. Use it from a deploy script, or from a system cron when DISABLE_WP_CRON is set, for example wp eval "do_action( 'sc_wpun_run_check' );".

There is no lock: a run that overlaps another check, scheduled or manual, can send an update the other is also sending, so it may arrive twice. A channel that must never deliver twice can keep its own record of what it sent.

do_action( 'sc_wpun_run_check' );

There is no capability check. Before firing it from anything a user can reach, check current_user_can() with the capability from the sc_wpun_capability filter.

Handled in includes/class-plugin.php.

docs.title: Item types and routing
docs.text: Out of the box a notification carries three kinds of item: core, plugin and theme. An add-on can report other things that need attention, such as a PHP version reaching end of life or a licence about to expire, by registering an item type and adding items of that type. Channel instances can then be routed to receive them or not.

docs.title: 1. Register the type
docs.text:
Use the sc_wpun_item_types filter. The key is lower case letters, digits and underscores, and the label is shown on the settings screen, where each instance's routing lists the registered types.

add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_item_types',
    function ( $types ) {
        $types['php'] = __( 'PHP', 'my-addon' );
        return $types;
    }
);

Invalid entries are dropped, and core, plugin and theme cannot be removed or renamed.

Registering the type matters for the delivery history. Once an item of a registered type is no longer returned by your filter, the plugin forgets what it told each instance about it, so the item is new again if it comes back. The history of an item whose type is not registered is never pruned: it grows, and an item that goes away and returns with the same new_version is not sent again.

docs.title: 2. Add items
docs.text:
Add WPUN\Notification_Item objects with the sc_wpun_update_items filter. It runs on every update check, after core, plugins and themes were collected.

add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_update_items',
    function ( $items ) {
        if ( version_compare( PHP_VERSION, '8.1', '<' ) ) {
            $items[] = new \WPUN\Notification_Item(
                array(
                    'type'            => 'php',
                    'key'             => 'php',
                    'name'            => 'PHP',
                    'current_version' => PHP_VERSION,
                    'new_version'     => '8.4',
                    'links'           => array( 'details' => 'https://www.php.net/supported-versions.php' ),
                    'notes'           => array( __( 'Your PHP version no longer gets security fixes.', 'my-addon' ) ),
                )
            );
        }
        return $items;
    }
);

How the item's fields are used:

  • type and key identify the item. Keep the key stable between runs.
  • new_version is what the history remembers. An instance is told about an item once per new_version: the same item with the same new_version is not sent again, and a different new_version is.
  • name, current_version, links and notes appear in the message.
  • flags are machine-readable facts (scalars) for routing rules and channels. They are not shown in the message.

Only Notification_Item objects survive the filter. The constructor throws an InvalidArgumentException for an invalid type.

docs.title: 3. Route it
docs.text:
Each instance's routing is an array kept in Channel_Instance::get_routing(). WPUN\Routing knows three keys:

Key Values Meaning types list of item types The types the instance receives. Empty or missing means every type, including yours. scope all, active For plugin and theme items: active keeps only items whose active flag is true. core all, major For core items: major keeps only updates that change the major.minor version.

Site owners choose these on the instance's form. Other keys are stored and ignored by the plugin, so instances defined in code (the SC_WPUN_CHANNELS constant or the sc_wpun_channels filter) can carry rules of your own.

For anything the three keys cannot express, use the sc_wpun_channel_should_receive_item filter. It runs after the instance's own rules, so it can block an item they let through or let through one they blocked:

add_filter(
    'sc_wpun_channel_should_receive_item',
    function ( $receive, $item, $instance ) {
        // Only the "security_team" instance gets PHP items, and it gets nothing else.
        if ( 'security_team' === $instance->get_id() ) {
            return 'php' === $item->get_type();
        }
        return 'php' === $item->get_type() ? false : $receive;
    },
    10,
    3
);

To stop an item from going anywhere, use sc_wpun_should_notify_item instead. A vetoed item still counts as waiting, so it is not sent again as new when you stop vetoing it.

docs.title: In a channel
docs.text: A channel receives only the items routed to its instance, in $notification->get_items(). get_items_of_type( 'php' ) picks one type. A channel that formats messages itself should cope with item types it does not know, since any add-on can add one. WPUN\Notification_Renderer lists every item the same way, whatever its type: name, versions, links and notes.

docs.title: Stability and deprecation
docs.text: From 2.0.0, the hooks and the module API are public API. This page says what that covers, how it changes, and how an add-on checks what it can use.

docs.title: What is public
docs.text:
• Every hook in the hook reference: its name, its arguments and what its return value does.
  • The functions sc_wpun_register_channel(), sc_wpun_channels(), sc_wpun_api_version(), sc_wpun_api_satisfies() and sc_wpun_api_supports(), and the SC_WPUN_API_VERSION constant.
  • The classes and methods in the WPUN namespace that are documented with @since and not tagged @internal. These include Channel, Channel_Instance, Channel_Registry, Channel_Store, Delivery_Result, Notification, Notification_Item, Notification_Renderer, Routing, Item_Types, Version_Constraint, Config_Source, Config_Context and Config_Value.
  • The names that configuration can be supplied under: SC_WPUN_SETTING_*, SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_<ID>__<FIELD>, SC_WPUN_CHANNELS and SC_WPUN_LOAD_FROM_ENV.
  • The field schema keys and field types described on WPUN\Channel, including 'secret' => true on a field of any type and show_external.
  • The security behaviour that add-ons rely on:
  • a secret is never rendered, and a field's renderer receives only '1' or '' for it;
  • var_dump() and print_r() of a Channel_Instance show [redacted] for every setting;
  • Notification_Item values are single lines, with control characters replaced by spaces;
  • Notification_Renderer::markdown() links only explicit http and https URLs.

Loosening any of these is a breaking change.

Anything tagged @internal can change or disappear in any release, even if it is declared public in PHP. That includes sc_wpun(), the classes that run the plugin (such as Plugin, Settings, State, Dispatcher, Update_Checker and Config), Field_Types (use the sc_wpun_field_types filter instead), and everything in WPUN\Admin. The layout of the options in the database is not public either: read and write instances through sc_wpun_channels().

The plugin's own modules in modules/ use only the public API, and CI enforces it with make check-public-api. If a module needs something that is not public, the API grows; the module does not reach inside.

docs.title: How it changes
docs.text:
• Breaking or removing a public hook, function, class or method needs a major version of the plugin.
  • Deprecating comes first. A deprecated hook goes through apply_filters_deprecated() or do_action_deprecated(), and a deprecated function or method calls _deprecated_function(), so WP_DEBUG shows a notice naming the replacement. It keeps working for at least one minor release before it can be removed in a major one.
  • Adding a hook, a method or an optional argument can happen in any minor release.

docs.title: The API version
docs.text:
The public API has its own semantic version, separate from the plugin's: SC_WPUN_API_VERSION, also returned by sc_wpun_api_version(). It started at 1.0.0 with plugin version 2.0.0.

  • A minor bump (1.0.0 to 1.1.0) adds API.
  • A major bump (1.x to 2.0.0) removes or changes some, following the deprecation rules above.

State the API versions your add-on works with as a version constraint, in any of three ways:

  • The Requires WPUN API plugin header, for example Requires WPUN API: ^1.0. WP Updates Notifier shows a notice below the add-on on the Plugins screen, before and after activation, when the site's API does not satisfy it or the value cannot be read. It does not block activation.
  • sc_wpun_api_satisfies() in your add-on's boot(), before using the API:
add_action(
    'plugins_loaded',
    function () {
        if ( ! function_exists( 'sc_wpun_api_satisfies' ) || ! sc_wpun_api_satisfies( '^1.0' ) ) {
            add_action( 'admin_notices', 'my_addon_needs_newer_updates_notifier' );
            return;
        }
        add_action( 'sc_wpun_register_channels', 'my_addon_register_channel' );
    }
);
  • Channel::get_api_constraint(), which the registry enforces (see below).

sc_wpun_api_satisfies() takes Composer's constraint syntax and nothing else. ^1.0 is true for any 1.x from 1.0.0 on, and false for 2.0.0, since a new major version may have removed what you use.

Constraint Meaning 1.2.0, =1.2.0 exactly >=1.0, >1.0, <2.0, <=1.4, !=1.3.0 comparison ^1.2 >=1.2.0 <2.0.0 (for ^0.x, Composer's rules) ~1.2 >=1.2.0 <2.0.0 ~1.2.3 >=1.2.3 <1.3.0 1.2.* >=1.2.0 <1.3.0 >=1.0 <1.4, >=1.0, <1.4 both (AND) ^1.0 \|\| ^2.0 either (OR)

Missing minor and patch parts count as 0. Pre-release suffixes are not supported, because the API version never has one. Other syntaxes, such as Ruby's ~> or a hyphen range, are invalid. An invalid constraint returns false, so a typo fails closed, and triggers _doing_it_wrong() once per constraint per request, so the developer sees why.

sc_wpun_api_supports( '1.2.0' ) still works. It is the ^ shorthand, the same as sc_wpun_api_satisfies( '^1.2.0' ), and takes a full X.Y.Z version only.

To check some other version against a constraint, call WPUN\Version_Constraint::satisfies( $version, $constraint ). Version_Constraint::is_valid( $constraint ) tells whether a constraint can be read, without a notice.

docs.title: Enforcement by the registry
docs.text:
A channel can declare the API versions it needs in Channel::get_api_constraint(), and the registry enforces it. When the site's API version does not satisfy the constraint, or the constraint cannot be read (which also triggers _doing_it_wrong()), Channel_Registry::register() returns false and fires sc_wpun_channel_rejected. Channel_Registry::get_rejected() lists the refused channels with the reason.

A site owner sees it in three places:

  • On the Channels tab, instances of the refused module are listed below the channels in an "Unavailable channels" table with "Unavailable: ..." and the reason. They cannot be edited, tested, switched, duplicated or deleted, and their settings are kept.
  • A notice on the plugin's own settings page (never site-wide) lists each refused module once.
  • Site Health shows a recommendation while a module is refused.

Updating WP Updates Notifier, or the add-on to a version that registers successfully, clears all of it. The check in your plugins_loaded callback is still needed for code that runs outside the channel and for your own notice. See Writing a module.

Also declare the dependency in your plugin header, so WordPress (6.5 and later) refuses to activate your add-on without WP Updates Notifier:

 * Requires Plugins: wp-updates-notifier

docs.title: Writing a notification module
docs.text:
A notification module adds a channel type: a new way of delivering update notifications, such as a chat service, an SMS gateway or a ticketing system. Site owners then create any number of instances of it on the Channels tab, each with its own settings and routing.

This guide builds one step by step. The finished result is the example add-on in examples/wpun-example-channel/, which posts to a chat webhook. Copy it as a starting point. Two more references:

  • modules/email/: the built-in email channel. It is written exactly like an add-on, using only the public API.
  • tests/fixtures/plugins/wpun-test-addon/: the test add-on, which exercises every extension point (custom field types, configuration sources, short-circuited sends).

docs.title: 1. The plugin file
docs.text:
A module is an ordinary WordPress plugin. Its header declares the dependency, so WordPress 6.5 and later will not activate it without WP Updates Notifier:

/**
 * Plugin Name:       My Chat Channel
 * Requires at least: 6.7
 * Requires PHP:      7.4
 * Requires Plugins:  wp-updates-notifier
 * Requires WPUN API: ^1.0
 */

Requires WPUN API is optional. It takes the same constraint syntax as sc_wpun_api_satisfies(), and WP Updates Notifier shows a notice below the add-on on the Plugins screen, before and after activation, when the site's API version does not satisfy it or the value cannot be read. It does not block activation.

Requires Plugins makes WordPress check that WP Updates Notifier is active, not its version. Three checks cover the version: the header (the Plugins screen notice), the boot check below (code outside the channel, with your own notice) and get_api_constraint() (the channel itself, enforced by the registry, see Declare the API version you need). Check the API version before using anything, and register the channel on the sc_wpun_register_channels action:

namespace My_Chat_Channel;

function boot(): void {
    if ( ! function_exists( 'sc_wpun_api_satisfies' ) || ! \sc_wpun_api_satisfies( '^1.0' ) ) {
        add_action( 'admin_notices', __NAMESPACE__ . '\\api_notice' );
        return;
    }

    require_once __DIR__ . '/class-my-chat-channel.php';

    add_action(
        'sc_wpun_register_channels',
        static function ( \WPUN\Channel_Registry $registry ) {
            $registry->register( new My_Chat_Channel() );
        }
    );
}
add_action( 'plugins_loaded', __NAMESPACE__ . '\\boot' );

sc_wpun_api_satisfies( '^1.0' ) is true for any 1.x API from 1.0.0 on. Ask for the oldest version that has everything you use, and use a wider constraint such as >=1.0 <3.0 only for versions you have tested. See Stability and deprecation.

The check in boot() is for everything outside the channel. The registry already checks the channel itself (see the next step), but only your code knows what else it does: hooks your add-on adds on its own, or its own settings screen, would still run against an API that is too old. Keep the explicit sc_wpun_api_satisfies() check for those, and for showing your own notice.

Do the work on plugins_loaded, not when the file is included. By then every active plugin is loaded, whatever order WordPress loaded them in.

docs.title: 2. The channel class
docs.text:
Extend WPUN\Channel. Three methods are required:

use WPUN\Channel;
use WPUN\Channel_Instance;
use WPUN\Delivery_Result;
use WPUN\Notification;

class My_Chat_Channel extends Channel {

    public function get_type(): string {
        return 'my_chat';
    }

    public function get_label(): string {
        return __( 'My Chat', 'my-chat-channel' );
    }

    public function send( Notification $notification, Channel_Instance $instance ): Delivery_Result {
        // See step 4.
    }
}
  • get_type() is the unique key of the channel: lower case letters, digits and underscores. Instances are stored under it, so never change it once people use your module. Registration fails (returns false) for an invalid or duplicate type.
  • get_label() is the name site owners pick from when adding a channel.

The optional methods:

Method Default Override to get_description() empty Describe the channel in one sentence on the "Add channel" screen. get_fields() no fields Describe the settings of an instance. See step 3. get_api_constraint() empty: no check Declare the API versions the channel needs, for example '^1.0'. The registry refuses the channel on a site whose API does not satisfy it. See "Declare the API version you need" below. supports( $feature ) false Return true for test_message to get a "Send test message" button. validate_settings( $settings, $stored ) checks every field against its schema Add checks that span several fields. Call parent::validate_settings() first. render_settings( $instance ) null: the form is drawn from the schema Draw the fields yourself. Rarely needed, and you then take over the accessibility of the fields: see Accessibility.

docs.title: Declare the API version you need
docs.text:
Override get_api_constraint() to say which API versions the channel works with. It takes the same constraint syntax as sc_wpun_api_satisfies():

public function get_api_constraint(): string {
    return '^1.0';
}

When the channel is registered, the registry checks the constraint against sc_wpun_api_version(). If it is not satisfied, or cannot be read, register() returns false, the channel is not available, and the sc_wpun_channel_rejected action fires. Site owners see "Unavailable: ..." for the channel's instances on the Channels tab, a notice on the plugin's settings page and a Site Health recommendation. Their settings are kept, so everything works again once WP Updates Notifier is updated. See Stability and deprecation.

docs.title: 3. Settings: the field schema
docs.text:
get_fields() returns an array keyed by setting name. The plugin draws the form on the Channels tab, validates what is submitted, stores it and supplies it to send() through the instance. You write no form, security token or saving code.

public function get_fields(): array {
    return array(
        'webhook_url' => array(
            'type'        => 'url',
            'label'       => __( 'Webhook address', 'my-chat-channel' ),
            'description' => __( 'The address the chat service gave you.', 'my-chat-channel' ),
            'required'    => true,
            'secret'      => true,
        ),
        'username'    => array(
            'type'  => 'text',
            'label' => __( 'Name to post as', 'my-chat-channel' ),
        ),
    );
}

The types are text, textarea, url, email_list, secret, number, boolean and enum (with checkbox and select as aliases). The full list of keys (default, required, secret, show_external, options, multiple, display, min, max, sanitize_callback, validate_callback and more) is documented on the WPUN\Channel class in includes/abstract-class-channel.php.

A field with 'required' => true is also marked in the form: "(required)" after its label (not for a boolean, which is always valid) and aria-required="true" on its control. For a group of radio buttons the fieldset gets role="radiogroup" to carry it; a group of checkboxes has only the text. A secret that already has a saved value keeps the text but not the attribute, as leaving it empty is valid. A custom field type registered with sc_wpun_field_types receives the schema in its render callable, so read required there and do the same.

Every instance also has a label, an on/off switch and routing. The plugin adds these; don't put them in get_fields().

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The default validate_settings() runs, for every field: its sanitize_callback, the sanitiser of its type, then required and its validate_callback. An error is a WP_Error whose data names the field, and the form shows it next to that field. Override validate_settings() only for rules that involve several fields:

public function validate_settings( array $settings, array $stored = array() ) {
    $clean = parent::validate_settings( $settings, $stored );
    if ( is_wp_error( $clean ) ) {
        return $clean;
    }
    if ( '' !== ( $clean['username'] ?? '' ) && '' === ( $clean['icon_url'] ?? '' ) ) {
        return new \WP_Error( 'invalid_field', __( 'Set an icon when you set a name.', 'my-chat-channel' ), array( 'field' => 'icon_url' ) );
    }
    return $clean;
}

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Mark anything that grants access as secret: API tokens, passwords, and webhook URLs that carry a token. Use the secret type, or 'secret' => true on a field of any type, including a custom one. A secret:

  • is never written back into the form once saved. The form shows that a value is saved, leaving the field empty keeps it, and a "Clear" checkbox empties it;
  • is never handed to the field's renderer: a custom type's render callable gets '1' as the value when one is saved and '' when not;
  • is still stored in the database in plain text, like other plugin settings. Site owners who want it out of the database can supply it from wp-config.php, an environment variable or a secrets service instead. See Configuration sources. Your fields support this automatically, for example SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_OPS_CHAT__WEBHOOK_URL.

A value that comes from outside the database (a constant, an environment variable or a source) is not printed on the edit screen for the text types (text, textarea, url, email_list) unless the field sets 'show_external' => true: the screen then only says "Set by ...". Flag secrets with secret, and set show_external only for harmless values such as an address or a name.

Instances that reach hooks and your send() hold the resolved settings, secrets included. var_dump() and print_r() of a Channel_Instance show the setting names with [redacted] values, but don't log or dump the settings yourself.

Your own code must keep secrets secret too. Never put one in a Delivery_Result message, an admin notice or a log. Results are shown to administrators and stored. The error messages of the HTTP API can contain the URL that was requested, so don't pass them on as they are.

docs.title: Custom field types
docs.text:
If none of the types fits, register one with the sc_wpun_field_types filter. Each entry has a render callable that returns the escaped markup of the control and a sanitize callable that returns the clean value or a WP_Error. The test add-on's test_colour type in class-test-form-channel.php is a complete example, and the hook reference documents both signatures.

Other plugins can add fields to your channel with sc_wpun_channel_fields. The fields your code receives are those of get_form_fields(), which applies that filter, so read settings by name and don't assume the list is only yours.

docs.title: 4. Delivering: send()
docs.text:
send() is called once per enabled instance, with a WPUN\Notification holding only the items routed to that instance and not yet delivered to it. Read the instance's settings with $instance->get_setting( 'name', $fallback ).

It must always return a WPUN\Delivery_Result:

return Delivery_Result::success();

return Delivery_Result::failure( $message, $code, $http_status, $retry_after, $context );

On success, the plugin records the items as delivered to this instance. On failure it records nothing, so the same items go out again on the next scheduled check. Other instances are not affected. The message of the latest result, success or failure, is shown on the Channels tab, so write it for the site owner: say what happened, in a sentence.

If send() throws, the dispatcher catches the exception, records a failure with the code exception and goes on with the other instances. Don't rely on it: catch what you expect and return a failure with a message the site owner can act on.

docs.title: The message
docs.text:
$notification gives you the site name and URL, the link to the Updates screen, the items (get_items(), each a WPUN\Notification_Item with name, versions, links and notes), and is_test() for a test message. WPUN\Notification_Renderer turns a notification into plain_text(), markdown() or html(), with the values escaped for that format. Use it unless your service needs something special. markdown() targets CommonMark (backslash escapes). A service with its own dialect, for example Slack mrkdwn, which ignores backslashes and needs &, < and > turned into entities, must escape for that dialect itself; a Slack renderer comes with the Slack module, not in 2.0.0. Links whose URL is not http or https are rendered as plain text. Site code can change the plain text with sc_wpun_message_text.

Pass what you are about to send through $this->filter_payload( $payload, $notification, $instance ). It applies the sc_wpun_channel_payload and sc_wpun_channel_payload_{type} filters, so site code can adjust your payload without forking your module. A filter can return anything, so check the result still has the shape you need. Document the shape of your payload for your users.

docs.title: HTTP
docs.text:
• Use wp_safe_remote_post() for any address a site owner typed in. It refuses addresses on the server's own network, which stops your webhook field from being used to reach internal services. Use wp_remote_post() only for your service's fixed API address. It also refuses ports other than 80, 443 and 8080. To try your module against a receiver on a local network, allow that host on your development site with the http_request_host_is_external filter. Don't ship that filter.
  • Set a short timeout (10 seconds or less). The check delivers to every instance in turn, during a cron request.
  • Check the HTTP status. A WP_Error or a status outside 2xx is a failure.
$response = wp_safe_remote_post(
    $url,
    array(
        'timeout' => 10,
        'headers' => array( 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' ),
        'body'    => wp_json_encode( $payload ),
    )
);

if ( is_wp_error( $response ) ) {
    return Delivery_Result::failure( __( 'The request to the webhook failed.', 'my-chat-channel' ), 'http_error' );
}

$status = (int) wp_remote_retrieve_response_code( $response );
if ( $status < 200 || $status >= 300 ) {
    return Delivery_Result::failure( sprintf( __( 'The webhook answered with HTTP %d.', 'my-chat-channel' ), $status ), 'bad_status', $status );
}

return Delivery_Result::success();

docs.title: Rate limits and retries
docs.text:
When the service answers HTTP 429, return a failure with the status and the wait from the Retry-After header. Delivery_Result::retry_after_from_response( $response ) reads it, as seconds or as an HTTP date, and gives null if there is none or it is not usable:

if ( 429 === $status ) {
    return Delivery_Result::failure(
        __( 'The webhook is limiting requests.', 'my-chat-channel' ),
        'rate_limited',
        429,
        Delivery_Result::retry_after_from_response( $response )
    );
}

A failure with a retry_after defers the instance: update checks skip it until that long after the failure, and its items stay unsent and go out on the first check after. Other instances are not affected, and nothing extra is scheduled. The plugin caps the wait at 7 days. A test send ignores the deferral and does not set it, and a later success, or a failure without retry_after, clears it. Without a retry_after, the items are retried on the next scheduled check, which is at least an hour away. Don't retry inside send(), and don't sleep.

docs.title: Length limits
docs.text:
Most services limit the size of a message. Respect the limit by sending a summary rather than a message the service will refuse. Notification_Renderer does this for you: pass the limits to plain_text(), markdown() or html().

$text = Notification_Renderer::plain_text( $notification, 4000, 50 );
  • $max_length is the longest result in characters, and $max_items the most items to list. 0 (the default) means no limit. Output is the same as without limits when everything fits.
  • The renderer lists the largest number of items that fits and adds a line "…and N more" (translatable, with a plural form) when some are left out. The line sits before the closing "Please visit…" line; in Markdown it follows the list after a blank line, in HTML it is a paragraph after the list. Nothing is added when no item is left out.
  • If even a message without any item is longer than $max_length, it is returned anyway (title, "more" line and closing line), never an empty string, so the result can then exceed the limit.
  • Lengths are characters (mb_strlen()). Some services count bytes or UTF-16 code units, so leave a margin or measure the result yourself.
  • Site code can change the "more" line with the sc_wpun_more_items_text filter (return plain text, it is escaped for the format). The sc_wpun_message_text filter still applies to plain text, and the length is measured after it. With a limit, it may run several times per message and receives the number of items left out as its third argument.

The example channel's message() method does this.

Bear in mind that a successful send counts every item as delivered, including the ones summarised as "…and N more". They are not sent again.

docs.title: Duplicate deliveries
docs.text: The plugin does not lock update checks against each other. If a check started with sc_wpun_run_check overlaps a scheduled one, both can send the same update before either records it, so a notification can occasionally arrive twice. For update notices that is a fair trade for a simpler plugin. If your service must never receive the same message twice, keep your own record in send(), for example the notification's item keys and versions per instance, and skip what you already sent.

docs.title: 5. Testing
docs.text:
The plugin's own tests show how to test a module with WordPress's PHPUnit test suite and mocked HTTP. tests/wp/test-example-channel.php tests the example add-on:

  • It loads the add-on's main file the way WordPress would, calls boot(), and registers the channel.
  • It answers HTTP requests with the pre_http_request filter, so no request leaves the machine, and it checks what was sent.
  • It covers success, an error status, a WP_Error, a 429 with and without Retry-After, the summary of a long list (by count and by length), and that no failure message contains the webhook URL.
  • It runs a whole update check to show a failed send is retried on the next run.

A minimal mocked request in your own tests:

add_filter(
    'pre_http_request',
    function ( $pre, $args, $url ) use ( &$sent ) {
        $sent = array( 'url' => $url, 'body' => json_decode( $args['body'], true ) );
        return array(
            'headers'  => array(),
            'body'     => '',
            'response' => array( 'code' => 200, 'message' => 'OK' ),
            'cookies'  => array(),
            'filename' => null,
        );
    },
    10,
    3
);

$result = ( new My_Chat_Channel() )->send( $notification, $instance );
$this->assertTrue( $result->is_success() );

Return a WP_Error from the filter to test a failed connection.

docs.title: Checking your code
docs.text:
You can run the plugin's own checks on your add-on:

  • Coding standards. Copy examples/wpun-example-channel/phpcs.xml.dist and change the text domain and prefixes. It is the WordPress ruleset, including the escaping, security token and sanitising sniffs, with the same PHP and WordPress versions as the plugin.
  • Semgrep. Run Semgrep CE with the plugin's rules on your code: semgrep scan --config path/to/wp-updates-notifier/.semgrep/ --metrics=off your-addon/. The rules ban eval, unserialize, $_REQUEST and unprepared $wpdb queries, and they require wp_safe_remote_* for HTTP. Your fixed API address may use wp_remote_post() with // nosemgrep: wpun-outbound-http-safe-only -- <reason>. The rules are GPL, like the plugin.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text: The settings screen is checked against WCAG 2.2 AA, and a module is part of it.

docs.title: Prefer schema fields
docs.text:
Fields drawn from get_fields() get the accessible markup for free:

  • a label for each control, or a fieldset with a legend for a group of radio buttons or checkboxes;
  • the description tied to the control with aria-describedby;
  • "(required)" after the label of a required field, and aria-required="true" on its control (a group of checkboxes only has the text; a saved secret keeps the text but not the attribute);
  • on an error, aria-invalid="true", the message under the field with a bold "Error:", and a summary at the top of the form with a link to each field. The link goes to the first control of a group of radio buttons or checkboxes;
  • a note on a saved secret ("A value is saved. Leave this empty to keep it, ..."), a clear checkbox named after the field, and a "Set by ..." note, tied to the control, for a value that comes from a constant or an environment variable.

A page title that starts with "Error:" after a failed save and the headings are the plugin's job too. Use render_settings() only when no schema field can do it.

docs.title: If you draw your own fields
docs.text:
Your markup gets none of the above, so it has to do it:

  • Give every control a <label for="...">. For a group of radio buttons or checkboxes use a <fieldset> with a <legend> instead.
  • Tie help text to its control with aria-describedby.
  • Start headings at <h4>: your markup sits under the form's <h3>Settings</h3>.
  • Never carry meaning by colour alone: say "Error:" or "(required)" in text. Check that the text is readable in forced-colours mode.

docs.title: Errors from custom markup
docs.text: Return errors from validate_settings() as a WP_Error keyed by field, as with schema fields (see Validation). The summary at the top of the form lists every message. It can only link to a control it knows, and with render_settings() it knows none, so the messages are listed without a link. Make your own controls show and announce the error: put the message next to the control, set aria-invalid="true" and point aria-describedby at the message.

docs.title: Choosing a display
docs.text:
• Use checkboxes rather than a select with multiple for a choice of several: a multiple select is hard to use with a keyboard and a screen reader.
  • Use radio buttons for a single choice of up to five options. The plugin does this by default and falls back to a select above five.

docs.title: Labels and text
docs.text:
• Labels are short, unique within the form and visible. Never use a placeholder as the label: it disappears when the user types.
  • In notification text avoid symbols such as arrows (read out as "right arrow" or not at all), and give a link a name that makes sense out of context, such as "Akismet changelog" rather than "Details". Notification_Renderer already writes "Akismet from version 5.6 to 5.7.2" and links named after the item; use it for the message, as the example channel does.

docs.title: Checking
docs.text: make a11y in the plugin repository runs axe and keyboard checks of the settings screen on a throwaway site, including a form with every field type. Also tab through your form and listen to it with a screen reader.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• The header has Requires Plugins: wp-updates-notifier and Requires WPUN API with the constraint, and boot() checks sc_wpun_api_satisfies( '^1.0' ) for code outside the channel.
  • get_api_constraint() returns the API versions the channel needs.
  • The type is unique and never changes.
  • Every credential is a secret field, and no secret reaches a message, notice or log.
  • send() always returns a Delivery_Result and never retries or sleeps.
  • HTTP uses wp_safe_remote_post() for user-supplied addresses, a short timeout and a status check.
  • 429 returns a failure with Retry-After.
  • Fields are schema fields where possible; custom markup has labels, described help text and its own error display (see Accessibility).
  • Long messages are summarised with "…and N more".
  • The payload goes through filter_payload().
  • Only the public API is used: nothing tagged @internal, not sc_wpun(), and not the plugin's options directly.

docs.title: Threat model for 2.0.0
docs.text:
What WP Updates Notifier trusts, where untrusted data crosses into it, what stops each threat, and the test or tool that proves the control holds. The security audit for 2.0.0 (#228) checks the code against this document, and the AI-assisted review (#230) reads it as context. When a change adds an entry point, a source of data or an outbound channel, update this document in the same pull request.

Threats are grouped by STRIDE: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service and Elevation of privilege. Tests are in tests/wp/. Tools are make targets, and CI runs each of them on every pull request (.github/workflows/). The security tests are in tests/wp/security/ (#220), and the OWASP ZAP scan is make dast (#222).

docs.title: Scope and assumptions
docs.text:
• WordPress core is trusted. That covers login, sessions, current_user_can(), security tokens (wp_verify_nonce()), options.php, wp_mail()/PHPMailer, the HTTP API's wp_safe_remote_* checks and the cron runner. A flaw in core is out of scope.
  • Administrators are trusted with what an administrator can already do in WordPress. Here that means anyone with the settings capability: manage_options by default, or whatever the sc_wpun_capability filter returns. On multisite that is a site administrator, and the plugin keeps settings per site.
  • Code that runs in the same PHP process is trusted. That covers other plugins, the theme, add-on channel modules, wp-config.php and anything hooked into the plugin's filters. Such code can already do anything the plugin can, so the public API does not try to sandbox it. What the plugin owes add-ons is a safe API when it is used as documented: secrets stay redacted, values are validated, and one broken module can't stop the others. See Public hook and add-on API.
  • Untrusted: every other user role, anyone not logged in, request parameters, plugin and theme headers written by third parties, data from api.wordpress.org, and responses from the services a channel sends to.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph untrusted["Untrusted"]
        anon["Visitors and users without the capability"]
        hdr["Plugin and theme headers"]
        wporg["api.wordpress.org"]
        svc["Services that channels send to"]
    end
    subgraph admin["Administrators (settings capability)"]
        browser["Browser: settings screen"]
    end
    subgraph process["WordPress PHP process (trusted code)"]
        cfg["wp-config.php constants, env vars, add-on sources, sc_wpun_config_value"]
        addon["Add-on modules and hook callbacks"]
        handlers["admin-post handlers and options.php save"]
        checker["Update_Checker (cron or on demand)"]
        renderer["Notification_Renderer: HTML, plain text, Markdown"]
        dispatcher["Dispatcher and channel modules"]
        db[("Options: sc_wpun_settings, sc_wpun_channels, sc_wpun_state")]
    end
    mail["Mail (wp_mail)"]

    anon -- "admin-post.php, options.php" --> handlers
    browser -- "POST + security token" --> handlers
    handlers --> db
    hdr -- "get_plugins(), wp_get_themes()" --> checker
    wporg -- "update_* site transients" --> checker
    db --> checker
    cfg --> checker
    checker --> renderer --> dispatcher
    addon --> dispatcher
    dispatcher -- "wp_mail()" --> mail
    dispatcher -- "wp_safe_remote_*" --> svc
    svc -- "status, Retry-After" --> dispatcher
    dispatcher --> db
    db -- "settings screen, Site Health" --> browser

The trust boundaries are:

  • the HTTP request into admin-post.php and options.php;
  • third-party data read from headers and transients;
  • outbound requests and the responses that come back;
  • the settings screen, where stored data is rendered.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: Asset Where it lives Why it matters Channel secrets (webhook URLs, tokens) sc_wpun_channels, or constants and env vars They let someone post into the site owner's chat or services. Recipient lists, From and Reply-To sc_wpun_channels Changing them redirects or spoofs the site's mail. Settings and schedule sc_wpun_settings, cron event sc_wpun_update_check Silencing them hides the updates a site needs. Delivery state sc_wpun_state It holds what was already notified, last_result and retry_at. The site's update inventory Sent in notifications It shows which outdated, possibly vulnerable, plugins a site runs. The release zip GitHub release, WordPress.org SVN A tampered build reaches every site that updates.

docs.title: 1. admin-post handlers
docs.text:
All are registered in Plugin::register_admin_hooks() (includes/class-plugin.php), except the Slack notice dismiss, which Plugin registers next to the notice. There are no admin_post_nopriv_*, wp_ajax_* or REST routes.

Action Handler Token action Method sc_wpun_send_test Channels_Tab::handle_test_send sc_wpun_send_test_<id> POST sc_wpun_channel_toggle Channels_Tab::handle_toggle sc_wpun_channel_toggle_<id> POST sc_wpun_channel_duplicate Channels_Tab::handle_duplicate sc_wpun_channel_duplicate_<id> POST sc_wpun_channel_delete Channels_Tab::handle_delete sc_wpun_channel_delete_<id> POST sc_wpun_check_now Check_Now::handle sc_wpun_check_now POST sc_wpun_save_channel Channel_Form::handle_save sc_wpun_save_channel_<new\|edit>_<type\|id> POST sc_wpun_dismiss_slack_notice Slack_Notice::handle_dismiss sc_wpun_dismiss_slack_notice GET (link)

Trust boundary: any HTTP client can reach admin-post.php. Unauthenticated requests fire only admin_post_nopriv_*, and the plugin registers none. The Semgrep rule wpun-no-nopriv-hooks (make sast, #216) fails the build if one is added.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof E A user without the capability changes channels, sends messages or runs the check. Each handler checks current_user_can( Settings_Page::capability() ) first, and refuses with a 403 and no change. test-channels-tab.php (test_nonce_and_capability_are_enforced_for_every_action), test-channel-form.php (test_nonce_and_capability_are_required, test_refusals_change_nothing, test_the_handler_answers_403_when_refused), test-check-now.php (test_a_refused_request_runs_nothing), test-test-send.php, test-slack-notice.php. security/test-capability-matrix.php (#220): discovers every admin_post_*/wp_ajax_* hook the plugin registers, fails on one without a request builder, and sends each one ten refused requests: logged out, subscriber, editor, administrator without manage_options, and administrator with no, empty, other-action, other-channel or other-user token, or the fields in the wrong method. Each must die with 403 and change nothing (options, user meta, mail, HTTP), with a positive control. The unauthenticated ZAP pass (make dast, #222). S/T CSRF: another site makes an administrator's browser post the action. A security token per action. Row actions and the form bind it to the channel id (and the mode and type), so a token for one channel can't act on another. The tests above. security/test-capability-matrix.php (#220) covers the wrong-action, other-channel and other-user tokens for every hook. T Tampered id, mode or type reaches the store. sanitize_key( wp_unslash() ) and is_string checks. Unknown ids and types are refused, and code-defined and externally set instances have no row actions. test-channels-tab.php, test-channel-form.php. T Open redirect after the action. Redirects use wp_safe_redirect() to the settings page. WPCS WordPress.Security.SafeRedirect (make lint). #222 checks the redirect targets. R An administrator denies changing a channel. Not addressed. WordPress has no audit log, and the plugin doesn't add one. Accepted for 2.0.0. n/a D Repeated Check now or test sends flood a mail service. Capability and security token limit this to administrators, who are trusted. As above.

The dismiss link is a GET that changes state, but only the current user's own meta (sc_wpun_dismissed_slack_notice). It still needs the security token and the capability.

docs.title: 2. The settings screen
docs.text:
The General tab saves through core's options.php (register_setting with sc_wpun_settings_validate, and option_page_capability_sc_wpun_settings returns the same capability). The Channels tab and the channel form use the handlers above. Field types are in includes/class-field-types.php, class-boolean-field.php and class-enum-field.php. They render through includes/admin/class-field-renderer.php.

Trust boundary: administrator input in, and stored, external and add-on data rendered back out.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof E Someone without the capability opens the page. Settings_Page::settings_page() refuses with a 403. Core's options.php checks the filtered capability. test-settings-screen.php (test_the_page_refuses_users_without_the_capability). T Invalid or hostile values are stored. Each field type sanitises and validates. Text uses sanitize_text_field. URLs need an http or https scheme and pass esc_url_raw. Email lists go through sanitize_email and is_email. Numbers are bounded, enums are allowlisted, and only declared fields are kept. Unknown notify keys and frequencies are refused. test-field-types.php, test-settings-validation.php, test-boolean-field.php, test-enum-field.php, test-field-showcase.php. security/test-settings-input.php (#220): hostile payloads through every field type, for the email schema and an add-on schema, and javascript:, data: and file: URLs. ZAP fuzzes the field showcase (make dast, #222). I Stored XSS through a field value, an error message or a channel's last result. Late escaping (esc_html, esc_attr, esc_url) in the renderer and tabs, checked by WPCS's WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput. Psalm follows options and transients to echo. test-settings-markup.php, test-channel-form.php (test_an_error_without_a_field_is_plain_text), make lint, make taint (#218). security/test-stored-xss.php (#220): payloads in every tab and form, the reflected tab, action, id and type parameters, and the channel list with its last result. I A secret is shown on the page. Secret fields are never rendered: the renderer only learns whether a value is saved ('1'/''). An empty input keeps the stored value, and <name>__clear removes it. secret => true works on any type. Values set in code show as read-only and are never echoed unless the schema opts in with show_external, which email uses for its non-secret fields only. test-field-types.php (test_render_secret_never_outputs_value, test_secret_keep_and_clear, test_secret_flag_on_other_types), test-channel-form.php (test_secrets_are_never_output_and_can_be_kept_or_cleared, test_secrets_are_not_kept_for_the_error_round_trip), test-channels-tab.php (test_duplicate_does_not_store_external_secrets). security/test-secrets.php (#220): a secret set through the form, a constant and an env var never shows, apart from the placeholder or its source. E An add-on schema renders unescaped markup. Add-on code is trusted (see Scope). Its custom render callbacks are its own responsibility. docs/developers/writing-a-module.md.

docs.title: 3. Update data
docs.text:
Plugin and theme names, versions, authors and URLs come from third-party headers (get_plugins(), wp_get_themes()) and from api.wordpress.org through the update_core, update_plugins and update_themes site transients (includes/class-update-checker.php). They become Notification_Item values and are rendered as HTML email, plain text or Markdown (includes/class-notification-renderer.php), as well as in the update nag and Site Health.

Trust boundary: third-party strings in, and markup out.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof T/I A plugin name such as <script>… or "><img onerror=…> runs in HTML mail or an admin page. Notification_Item collapses control characters so each value is a single line. The HTML renderer escapes every value with esc_html or esc_url. Markdown escapes its special characters and links only explicit http(s) URLs. Plain text is not HTML, and it is sent as text/plain. test-notification.php (test_html_escapes_values, test_markdown_escapes_special_characters, test_markdown_drops_unsafe_link_targets, test_plain_text_is_not_escaped), test-message-snapshot.php, make taint (sources get_plugins, get_plugin_data, wp_get_themes, get_site_transient). security/test-stored-xss.php (#220): the payloads through a mocked update check into the HTML and plain-text mail (no live markup, no double encoding), the nag, the channel list, Site Health and every tab. T A javascript: link in a header reaches a notification. esc_url in HTML, and the http(s)-only rule in Markdown. test-notification.php. security/test-stored-xss.php (#220). D Huge or many items blow a channel's size limit. Renderer limits truncate and summarise. test-renderer-limits.php. I The update inventory leaks to someone who shouldn't see it. It goes only to recipients and channels an administrator set up. The hide_updates setting removes the nag for users who can't update_core. test-update-nag.php, test-routing.php.

Two things the security tests found are out of scope or accepted:

  • WordPress core's own update nag prints the update_core version without escaping. That is core's output, not the plugin's, and the plugin adds nothing to the nag.
  • A right-to-left override (U+202E) in a plugin name survives into the mail and the admin. It can make a name display misleadingly, but it can't inject markup. Accepted.

docs.title: 4. Configuration sources
docs.text:
Any setting or channel field can come from a wp-config.php constant (SC_WPUN_SETTING_<NAME>, SC_WPUN_CHANNEL_<ID>__<FIELD>) or from an environment variable. Environment variables are off unless SC_WPUN_LOAD_FROM_ENV or the sc_wpun_load_from_env filter turns them on. Add-ons can register sources with sc_wpun_config_sources, and the sc_wpun_config_value filter has the last word (includes/class-config.php).

Trust boundary: none to the outside. All of these are server-side and trusted. The risks are values that are malformed or leak.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof T A malformed value breaks a channel or bypasses validation. Every value is cast to the field's type and validated like form input. A rejected value is not used anywhere and is listed, without the value, in Site Health. A throwing or junk source is skipped. test-config.php (test_precedence_for_a_setting, test_a_throwing_source_is_skipped, test_a_junk_source_is_dropped), test-config-channels.php (test_a_rejected_value_is_not_used_anywhere). I A secret from wp-config or the environment shows up in a page, a log, Site Health or debug output. Config_Value hides secret values in debug output and string casts. Channel_Instance::__debugInfo redacts. Reports name only the source, never the value. External values are read-only on the form. test-config-channels.php (test_a_secret_never_leaks, test_a_valid_secret_is_used_and_not_logged), test-config.php (test_external_settings_render_read_only). security/test-secrets.php (#220): Site Health debug data, _doing_it_wrong messages, notices, the debug log and print_r/var_dump of an instance. E An add-on uses the source API to override another plugin's values. Add-ons are trusted (see Scope). The order of precedence is documented and fixed. docs/developers/configuration-sources.md.

docs.title: 5. Outbound requests
docs.text:
Email is the only built-in channel, and it sends with wp_mail(). HTTP channels come from add-ons. The example add-on (examples/wpun-example-channel/) shows the expected pattern: wp_safe_remote_post(), a timeout, and Delivery_Result failures that leave out the address. Retry-After from a response is parsed by Delivery_Result::retry_after_from_response(). It is capped at 7 days (State::MAX_RETRY_AFTER), and it defers only that instance.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof I/E SSRF: a channel URL points at 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or the LAN. wp_safe_remote_* refuses private and loopback hosts unless the site allows them with core's http_request_host_is_external filter. URL fields accept only http(s). The Semgrep rule wpun-outbound-http-safe-only refuses wp_remote_* and other HTTP clients in the plugin and the example. Psalm treats wp_safe_remote_* URLs as SSRF sinks. make sast (#216), make taint (one baselined, reviewed finding in the example add-on), test-example-channel.php. security/test-outbound-requests.php (#220): every request of the example add-on carries reject_unsafe_urls. Loopback, link-local (metadata), private and IPv6 loopback addresses are refused, and only a host the site allows passes. The email module makes no HTTP request. D A service answers Retry-After: 99999999 or garbage and silences the channel for good. The header is parsed strictly, the wait is capped at a week, and the cap is per instance. test-retry-after.php. I An error message or last_result leaks the webhook URL. The example's failures leave out the address, and the module guide tells add-ons never to put a secret in a result, notice or log, nor to pass on the HTTP API's error messages as they are. test-example-channel.php (test_a_wp_error_is_a_failure_without_the_address). security/test-secrets.php (#220) checks last_result and the delivery state. T Mail header injection through the From name, the subject, the recipients or the payload filters. Recipients and header lines with CR or LF are dropped after the payload filters (Email_Channel::checked_payload). The subject is built from sanitize_text_field values, and PHPMailer encodes it. From and Reply-To are validated email settings. test-hooks.php (header lines with line breaks are dropped), test-email-channel.php. #228 re-checks this by hand.

docs.title: 6. Public hook and add-on API
docs.text:
Add-ons register channel modules, item types and config sources, and they hook the documented actions and filters (docs/developers/hooks.md). Modules declare the API version they need, and a module that needs a newer one is refused, with a notice for administrators.

What an add-on is trusted to do: run any PHP, read and send its own channel's settings, change payloads through the filters, and supply config values. What the plugin still guarantees when an add-on is used as documented:

  • a module's secrets are never rendered or logged by the plugin;
  • schema values are sanitised and validated before the module sees them;
  • an exception in one module becomes a failed Delivery_Result and doesn't stop the other channels;
  • payload filters can't inject mail headers (see 5);
  • the capability for the screens comes from one filter, sc_wpun_capability, and a non-string or empty value falls back to manage_options.

Proof: test-extension-api.php, test-dispatcher.php, test-channel-api-constraint.php, test-api-version.php, test-contract.php, make check-public-api (modules use only the public API), and make check-hooks (every hook is documented).

docs.title: 7. Cron and on-demand runs
docs.text:
sc_wpun_update_check (WP-Cron) and sc_wpun_run_check (on demand, for example from WP-CLI) both run Update_Checker. Check now (1) calls the same code after its capability and security token checks.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof D/T Overlapping runs, such as cron and Check now together, deliver the same update twice. Accepted trade-off: there is no lock. A duplicate message is harmless, and a lock adds failure modes, such as a stale lock that silences notifications. n/a (recorded decision) E Anyone triggers a run. Visitors can only trigger WP-Cron at its schedule, never on demand. sc_wpun_run_check is an action for trusted code only. test-run-check.php, test-scheduling.php, test-check-now.php.

docs.title: 8. Stored data
docs.text:
These options are stored per site: sc_wpun_settings, sc_wpun_settings_ver, sc_wpun_channels and sc_wpun_state. There is also user meta for notices and form round trips. Secrets are stored in plain text in the options table, like every WordPress plugin's. Anyone who can read the database or run code can read them. A site that wants them out of the database sets them in wp-config.php constants or environment variables (4).

STRIDE Threat Control Proof I Secrets leak through var_dump, print_r or debug plugins. Channel_Instance::__debugInfo and Config_Value redact. test-notification.php, test-config-channels.php. I Data is left behind after uninstall. uninstall.php deletes every option, transient, user meta key and cron event, on every site of a network. test-uninstall.php, make test-dist (install, activate, deactivate, uninstall). T Options changed directly or by another plugin hold invalid data. Values are checked again when read: the store skips invalid instances and missing settings get their defaults. test-channel-store.php (test_invalid_entries_are_skipped_on_read), test-settings-state.php (test_missing_settings_get_defaults).

docs.title: 9. Build and release
docs.text:
The release zip is built by bin/build-dist.sh from the files .distignore doesn't exclude, and the build is reproducible. release-please opens the release PR with a GitHub App token and, when it is merged, makes a draft release with no tag. The release job then runs in the release environment, which is limited to main and needs the maintainer's approval. It builds the zip and its SBOM, attests the zip's provenance and SBOM, creates a signed annotated tag at the release commit, uploads the assets and publishes the release. The WordPress.org deploy (#57, not built yet) will run on the published release in the wordpress-org environment, which needs a reviewer.

STRIDE Threat Control Proof T A malicious or compromised workflow, action or tool image. Actions and tool images are pinned by digest. Workflows default to permissions: {} or read-only, and credentials aren't persisted. CODEOWNERS covers .github/ and bin/. Dependabot waits 14 days before proposing a new release. make check-workflows (actionlint, zizmor, #210), OpenSSF Scorecard (#224). T A vulnerable dependency. Runtime code has no dependencies (make dist-check enforces it). Development dependencies are audited. make audit (composer audit, OSV-Scanner), dependency review on PRs, make audit-images (Trivy), all #214. I A committed secret. Secrets live outside the repo. gitleaks scans the history, the tree and the zip. make secrets (gitleaks, #212). T Unreviewed changes on main. Branch protection: PRs, signed commits, linear history and the required checks. Scorecard Branch-Protection (#224). The accepted gaps are in SECURITY.md. S/T A tampered zip on GitHub. The zip is reproducible from the tag. The release job attests its build provenance and its SBOM, and checks the attestation before it publishes. make dist-repro on every PR, gh attestation verify in the release job (#226). S/T A forged or moved release tag. Tags are annotated and signed with a dedicated SSH key, held in the release environment. The v* ruleset forbids updating or deleting them. A re-run reuses the tag only if it points at the release commit and its signature checks out against .github/release-signers. make test-release (bin/sign-release-tag.sh), the release tags ruleset (#224, #226). S/T A tampered zip on WordPress.org. Not yet. Planned: the deploy runs only after the attestation of the zip it deploys checks out. #57.
